Benchling’s mission is to unlock the power of biotechnology. The world’s most innovative biotech companies use Benchling’s R&D Cloud to power the development of breakthrough products and accelerate time to milestone and market.

drive the integration of liquid biopsy approaches within the context of our portfolio, provide input into the clinical trial protocols

En tant qu’apprentie ou apprenti gestionnaire en hôtellerie-intendance, vous êtes amené ou amenée à découvrir et à exercer de nombreuses activités au sein de différents secteurs de l’institution. Vous participez aux travaux de nettoyage et d’entretien, au service des repas et des boissons, à la gestion du linge, à l’accueil des patients à la réception ainsi qu’à certaines activités de préparation en cuisine. Vous réalisez également diverses tâches administratives, notamment liées à la gestion des stocks et aux commandes.
La diversité des missions proposées et les exigences propres au milieu hospitalier vous permettent de bénéficier d’une formation complète et variée, favorisant le développement de compétences tant techniques que relationnelles. Afin d’enrichir votre parcours, des stages externes sont organisés pour vous permettre de découvrir d’autres domaines d’activité, notamment la gestion professionnelle d’une lingerie.
Au fil de votre apprentissage, vous développez votre sens du service, votre autonomie et votre polyvalence, tout en acquérant les compétences nécessaires à l’exercice du métier, conformément aux objectifs de votre formation.

À la Clinique de Crans-Montana, l’équipe de cuisine prépare chaque jour environ 180 repas destinés aux patientes et patients ainsi qu’au personnel de l’institution. Elle propose également une offre de petite restauration à la cafétéria. Sa mission est de garantir une alimentation équilibrée, variée et savoureuse, répondant aux recommandations nutritionnelles suisses et élaborée dans le respect des normes d’hygiène et de sécurité alimentaire. Labellisé « Cuisinons notre région » et « Fourchette verte », le service privilégie les produits frais et locaux afin de valoriser les saveurs du terroir.
En tant qu’apprenti ou apprentie cuisinière, vous participez à la préparation et à la réalisation de plats destinés à une clientèle variée, tout en tenant compte des régimes alimentaires spécifiques liés au milieu hospitalier.
La diversité des prestations et les exigences propres à notre environnement de soins vous permettent de bénéficier d’une formation riche et complète. Vous découvrez l’ensemble des postes de la cuisine et développez progressivement vos compétences techniques et organisationnelles.
Au cours de votre formation, vous apprenez les techniques de préparation et de cuisson des aliments, les règles d’hygiène et de sécurité alimentaire, ainsi que les bases de l’organisation et de la gestion d’une cuisine professionnelle, conformément aux objectifs de votre cursus.

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire d’un titre de spécialiste en pneumologie, vous assurez l’ensemble des activités cliniques du service et évoluez dans un environnement universitaire, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. Grâce à un tournus trimestriel au sein des différentes unités spécialisées, vous développez une expertise diversifiée couvrant aussi bien la pratique hospitalière qu’ambulatoire en faisant preuve de polyvalence. Vous intervenez notamment dans la prise en charge des pneumopathies interstitielles, des complications pulmonaires chez les patientes ou patients immunodéprimés, de la transplantation pulmonaire, de la pneumologie interventionnelle ainsi que des troubles respiratoires du sommeil, en collaboration étroite avec le Centre de médecine du sommeil.
Vous rejoignez une équipe soudée composée de 9 chefs et cheffes de clinique, 4 médecins adjoints et adjointes et 5 médecins internes, sous la responsabilité de la professeure cheffe de service. Vous collaborez étroitement avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire regroupant infirmiers et infirmières spécialisées, techniciens et techniciennes en physiologie respiratoire, personnel administratif ainsi que les différents centres et départements médicaux de l’institution.
Vous assurez la prise en charge diagnostique et thérapeutique des pathologies respiratoires aiguës et chroniques. Vous participez à l’évaluation et au suivi de situations complexes, incluant notamment la dyspnée, la tuberculose, l’insuffisance respiratoire et les différents domaines médico-techniques de la spécialité.
Vous faites preuve de résilience, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes. Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre capacité à prioriser, vous assurez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux multiples sollicitations (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions). Vous veillez à maintenir une communication claire, bienveillante et adaptée avec les patients et patientes, leurs proches ainsi qu’avec l’ensemble des professionnels impliqués dans leur prise en charge, en adaptant votre discours à leur compréhension.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du département de médecine dans le domaine de la pneumologie, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.

Pour renforcer son équipe, le Département des neurosciences cliniques recherche son ou sa future stagiaire dans le domaine de la qualité et sécurité des soins. 
Vous intégrez l’équipe qualité des neurosciences cliniques et vous participez aux projets en cours. Un membre de l'équipe est garant de votre intégration et apprentissage tout au long de votre mission.
Lors de votre stage, vous participez aux activités relevant du domaine de la qualité et sécurité des soins. Également, vous êtes amenée ou amené à mettre en place les projets du département sur ce domaine.

Introduction:
The Engineering Department (EN) pushes the boundaries of technology to enable physicists to carry out world-class scientific research. Within the EN Department, the Cooling and Ventilation Group (EN-CV) is responsible for the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the cooling and ventilation installations that support CERN's accelerators, experimental facilities, and technical infrastructure.
Within EN-CV, the Controls Section (EN-CV-CL) is responsible for the specification, development, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the industrial control systems used across all EN-CV installations.
The EN-CV control systems are based on industrial technologies, including Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, the UNICOS framework developed at CERN, automated code generation tools, and virtual commissioning methodologies. More than 650 PLCs are currently deployed and operated across EN-CV facilities, requiring a very high level of reliability, availability, and maintainability.
As a Controls Engineer, you will be involved in the full lifecycle of industrial control systems, from defining requirements and technical specifications to designing and implementing control solutions.
Functions:
Define control system requirements and produce functional specifications for cooling and ventilation installations.
Select and apply appropriate control and automation strategies to meet operational, reliability, and energy efficiency objectives.
Design, develop, test, and validate PLC application software for cooling and ventilation installations, ensuring compliance with applicable EN-CV-CL standard solutions and CERN UNICOS framework.
Configure, test, commission, maintain, and upgrade industrial control systems throughout their lifecycle.
Collaborate with project leaders, process engineers, operators, and other stakeholders throughout all project phases.
Coordinate technicians and junior engineers and supervise contractors during implementation and commissioning activities.
Manage technical procurements, service contracts, and interactions with industrial suppliers.
Provide expert operational support and troubleshooting for cooling and ventilation control systems.
Evaluate emerging technologies and engineering methodologies, and contribute to technical studies internal EN-CV-CL standards improvement.
Produce and ensure that technical documentation is complete, structured and up to date, in line with quality standards.

Introduction

Support Muon detector teams in coordinating LS3 activities to ensure timely delivery and efficient planning.
Prepare and maintain comprehensive documentation, progress reports, and activity summaries.

Join CERN's EP-ESE-ME section in the development of a radiation-tolerant microcontroller ASIC for use in future particle physics detectors and accelerator systems. Operating in highly challenging radiation environments, these systems require robust and reliable embedded electronics.
The project is based on an open-source RISC-V processing core and the CERN SOCRATES (System-On-Chip Radiation-Tolerant Ecosystem) framework for fault-tolerant SoC design. The successful candidate will contribute to the full development cycle, from requirements definition and system architecture to implementation, verification, and post-silicon validation.
Your responsibilities:
Analyse application requirements across CERN's accelerator complex and particle physics detector systems to define technical specifications for the microcontroller ASIC.
Contribute to the architecture, design, and validation of a radiation-tolerant microcontroller ASIC implemented in 65 nm or 28 nm CMOS technology.
Support the definition of the SoC architecture, including the selection and configuration of an appropriate RISC-V processing core.
Design, integrate, and validate peripheral IP blocks within the CERN SOCRATES framework.
Apply fault-tolerant design methodologies, including triple modular redundancy (TMR) and single-event upset (SEU) mitigation techniques.
Participate in design verification activities and physical implementation, from RTL development through to tapeout.
Contribute to post-silicon testing, characterisation, and validation following chip fabrication.
Your profile:
Strong understanding of digital logic design.
Solid experience with digital IC design and RTL development (Verilog/SystemVerilog).
Familiarity with standard ASIC design flows (synthesis, place and route, timing closure).
Knowledge of RISC-V architecture and its ecosystem.
Experience with microcontroller-based embedded systems development, including firmware programming in C and peripheral interfacing.
Skills:
RTL design and simulation (Verilog / SystemVerilog).
Familiarity with the digital ASIC design flow, including synthesis, place-and-route, timing closure, and sign-off activities.
Knowledge of fault-tolerant design techniques and radiation effects in CMOS circuits is an asset.
Microcontroller embedded systems development (firmware in C, peripheral interfacing, bare-metal programming).
Scripting and automation (Python or equivalent).
Linux/Unix working environment.
Curiosity and willingness to learn in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to work independently as well as within a team.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Please provide at least 1 reference letter to support your application.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Electronics Engineer (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

 - Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

 - Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

 - Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

 - Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

 - Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

 - Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

 - Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

 - Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

Functions

We are offering a position in the Physics Software Engineering section of the Computing for Experiments group in the CERN IT department (IT-CE-PSE) on Performance Software Engineering in the realm of high energy physics data simulation.
The work on this post will be carried out in the context of the NextGen project, a collaboration between the LHC experiments and the CERN Research and Computing Departments. NextGen explores the use and impact of high-performance computing architectures in data simulation and data processing for the LHC experiments with a focus on the upcoming High Luminosity (HL-LHC) data taking phase at the CERN Large Hadron Collider.
The simulation of particle collisions is one of the main consumers of computing resources for LHC experiments. Given the expected increase in the required statistics, accuracy and complexity for future simulation, and to stay within the forecasted computing budget, the throughput of simulation software packages needs to increase substantially.
The successful candidate will join a team of software engineers and physicists that addresses this challenge. Together, you will speed up software packages for Monte Carlo (MC) event generation with a focus on the Madgraph event generator suite. Current and future tasks tackled by the team are at the intersection of theoretical/computational physics and computer science. In order to profit from the latest computing hardware, adaptations or re-engineering of software in aspects such as data structures, parallelisation of the workflow or task scheduling are needed. This work is guided by the requirements of experimental analyses and takes into account the latest developments in theoretical predictions.
In case of interest, training on data science, programming languages, software engineering concepts and computing architectures is available and can be provided via various training programs.
Your responsibilities:
Analyse and profile existing simulation code bases and develop strategies for improving their throughput.
Implement latest software engineering concepts, leveraging on compute accelerators such as GPUs, modern CPU architectures and heterogeneous compute platforms.
Interact and collaborate with experts in the theory, experimental physics and software engineering communities at CERN and world-wide.
Supervise students on software development tasks and projects.

The next generation of experiments, the HL-LHC upgrade of CMS and the Future Circular Collider, needs event reconstruction that is fast, accurate and portable across CPUs and GPUs. Every reconstruction algorithm and every machine-learning model is trained and judged against the simulation truth. Today that truth is stored in static, detector-specific objects. Each object is pre-grouped for one purpose, it cannot be navigated, and it separates calorimeter truth from tracker truth.
CERN has built a prototype that replaces them. It is one navigable, event-level graph of the generator and simulation history, with calorimeter and tracker hit indices on top. Reconstruction code then reasons in terms of stable physics abstractions: particles, vertices, decay branches and hits.
You will make this the truth model of the future. You will generalise the prototype into an experiment-independent library, you will bring it into the FCC software stack, and you will use it to build the next reconstruction: graph algorithms and modern machine learning for clustering, particle flow and particle identification, and reliable matching between reconstructed objects and truth. You will join the EP-FCC group, and you will work on both CMS and FCC-ee.
Your responsibilities:
Generalise the CMS MC-truth graph into a detector-independent and experiment-independent library. Separate the graph data model, the navigation API and the hit index from the experiment data-format bindings.
Develop the bindings. Keep the CMSSW binding working, and add a binding for the FCC stack (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi), so that both experiments build the same graph from their own simulation output.
Extend the data model. Add multi-surface boundary crossings, sparse association storage, and a reduced hit-index layout. Handle pileup consistently.
Develop the reconstruction-to-truth association. Extend the adaptive branch associator, which selects the truth level that best matches a reconstructed object, and validate it on merged topologies such as converted photons, bremsstrahlung and early hadronic interactions.
Define what is reconstructible. Derive it from the truth graph and the detector description, using cell granularity, energy and time resolution, readout thresholds and two-object separation.
Apply portable graph algorithms and advanced machine learning, for example graph neural networks and transformers, to reconstruction tasks in CMS (HGCAL and TICL) and in FCC detectors: clustering, linking, particle flow and particle identification.
Build the training datasets and the labels from the truth graph. Define the metrics, calibrate the model outputs, and check the model before it feeds reconstruction.
Contribute the code to the official repositories of CMS and of the FCC software stack, with unit tests, documentation and code review.
Present the results in CMS and FCC meetings, in software forums and in publications.
This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
Your profile:
A Master's Degree or a PhD in Physics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics or a related field.
Demonstrated experience with modern C++ in a large, shared and peer-reviewed codebase, for example CMSSW, Gaudi or Key4hep.
Demonstrated experience with time-aware event reconstruction and detector simulation in a high-energy physics experiment.
Demonstrated experience with heterogeneous and portable computing, for example Alpaka, SYCL, CUDA or HIP.
Experience with Python and with at least one machine-learning framework, preferably PyTorch.
Experience with graph and clustering algorithms.
Experience with git, code review and continuous integration.

Detector simulation.
